caption: The drawing depicts the façade of a bell tower composed of three vertical sections. The structure has a rectangular lower base textured with small, dark, horizontal marks to suggest a stone or brick surface, and two upper levels each featuring arched openings for bells. The lowest visible portion of the tower contains three tall arches, the middle section has two arches, and the topmost portion has a single arched opening with a triangular pediment above it. The overall shape of the structure narrows as it rises, with horizontal lines separating each level. The drawing is rendered in shades of black and gray on a plain off-white background, using fine dot and line work for texture and shading. At the bottom left of the image, there is a ribbon-like banner with the year "1769" and the inscription "mission san diego de alcala" written in a neat, cursive style.
title: Mision San Diego de Alcala
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
